sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface ELISA against the N-terminal FLAG tag confirmed cell-surface expression (L3). Antibody-feeding internalisation assay confirmed normal receptor trafficking (L4). Reporter-gene assays with the N-terminal FLAG ADGRA3 construct characterised receptor signalling (L7). Receptor function preserved across all assays.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the 3×FLAG tag is placed between the signal peptide and residue 34 of the full-length membrane-anchored receptor, pinning the junction to insert_after_residue=33 (the last residue of the signal peptide, canonical numbering). Python lookup confirms seq[33]='G' and seq[34]='G'. The tag is therefore on the extracellular face of the large N-terminal ectodomain (residues 34–761), well clear of TM1 (762–783). Multiple independent papers (L2–L4, L6, L7) corroborate the same N-terminal position with FLAG or Myc tags, and L3/L4 directly demonstrate surface accessibility and normal trafficking. L1 (PMC9539791) reports a 3×FLAG tag inserted explicitly 'between a signal peptide and the full-length protein (amino acid residues 34–1321)' in a membrane-anchored FLAG–GPR125-FL construct expressed in MDCK cells. GPR125 is the approved alias for ADGRA3 (same UniProt entry Q8IWK6). L3 (PMC6899654) confirms cell-surface display of the N-terminal FLAG tag by ELISA under non-permeabilised conditions in HEK293 cells. L4 (PMC6899654) confirms receptor trafficking via antibody-feeding internalisation assay targeting the same N-terminal FLAG. L7 (PMC12059339) independently reports an N-terminal FLAG tag on a full-length ADGRA3 construct used in reporter-gene signalling assays, directly naming ADGRA3.

sources.claim: We next transfected MDCK cells with the complementary DNA (cDNA) for wild-type human GPR125 (FLAG–GPR125-FL), in which the 3 × FLAG-tag was inserted between a signal peptide and the full-length protein (amino acid residues 34–1321) ( Fig. 1 A ).

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines converge on a single extracellular site: the N-terminus of the mature protein (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 33). L1 is the most explicit, naming residues 34–1321 as the full-length span and placing the 3×FLAG between the SP and residue 34. L2–L4 and L6 corroborate the same N-terminal position on GPR125/ADGRA3 with FLAG or Myc tags. L7 directly names ADGRA3 with an N-terminal FLAG. No ledger line reports any insertion in an extracellular loop (ECL1 817–826, ECL2 898–916, ECL3 1018–1024) or anywhere else in the large ectodomain (34–761) other than the N-terminal junction. The C-terminal tags in L5 (2×V5) and L7 (1D4) are placed at the protein C-terminus, which falls in the intracellular C-tail (residues 1046–1321 per topology landmarks) and are therefore recorded in other_positions only.

literature_other_positions.note: L5 (PMC13631675) reports two V5 tags at the C-terminus of full-length GPR125/ADGRA3; the C-terminus (residues 1046–1321) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag is not on the extracellular face.
L7 (PMC12059339) reports a C-terminal 1D4 tag on full-length ADGRA3; the C-terminus lies in the intracellular C-tail (1046–1321) and is not surface-accessible.
